events.title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
events.description: British troops marched to seize colonial military supplies in Concord, Massachusetts, and clashed with colonial militia at Lexington and Concord. The first shots of the American Revolutionary War were fired, famously called the 'shot heard round the world.'
events.significance: Marked the outbreak of armed conflict in the American Revolutionary War, leading to American independence and the founding of the United States.

events.title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising Begins
events.description: Jewish insurgents in the Warsaw Ghetto launched an armed revolt when German forces entered to deport the remaining residents to extermination camps. Poorly armed fighters resisted for nearly a month until the ghetto was crushed in May.
events.significance: It was the largest single revolt by Jews during World War II and became a lasting symbol of resistance against Nazi persecution and the Holocaust.

events.title: Oklahoma City Bombing
events.description: Timothy McVeigh detonated a truck bomb outside the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, killing 168 people, including 19 children, and injuring hundreds more.
events.significance: It was the deadliest domestic terrorist attack in U.S. history, prompting major changes in federal building security and counterterrorism legislation.

events.title: Death of Charles Darwin
events.description: English naturalist Charles Darwin died at Down House in Kent at age 73. He was honored with a state funeral and buried in Westminster Abbey near Isaac Newton.
events.significance: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection, set out in On the Origin of Species, fundamentally transformed biology and our understanding of life.

events.title: Launch of Salyut 1
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Salyut 1, the world's first space station, into low Earth orbit. It later hosted the crew of Soyuz 11, who tragically died during reentry in June 1971.
events.significance: Salyut 1 began the era of long-duration human spaceflight and paved the way for later stations such as Mir and the International Space Station.
